messages:
Alex: PR #5223 ready for merge — adaptive-batching. Microbench shows slight tail latency increase on longseq (p99 +4%). Need quick reviews + decision before tomorrow's 10:00 UTC deploy window. bench results: https://ci.internal/bench/5223 :thinking_face:

Maria: can you paste the percentiles here? link sometimes hides numbers for me.

Alex: paste from the bench run (canary-sim):
```
p50: 12.0ms -> 12.1ms (+0.8%)
p90: 28.0ms -> 29.9ms (+6.8%)
p99: 145.0ms -> 151.0ms (+4.1%)
RSS baseline: 9.3GB -> 9.9GB (+6.5%)
```

Alex: tl;dr change is the default microbatch wait bumped. commit abc123 changed the default from 5ms -> 10ms. diff snippet:
```diff
- microbatch_wait_ms = 5
+ microbatch_wait_ms = 10
```

bench-bot: Ran bench on infra=canary-sim, model=longseq, seq=2048, concurrent=12; config: batching=adaptive, microbatch_wait=10ms; results: p99=151ms, p90=29.9ms, p50=12.1ms, RSS=9.9GB.

ci-bot: CI checks: unit tests ✅  integration ✅  smoke ✅  (build 5223-7)

Jordan: quick q — is canary-sim identical to prod canary (malloc/jemalloc, kernel, NUMA)? also did this PR touch kv-cache?

Alex: kv-cache not touched here. This is purely batching heuristic + default. canary-sim is mostly similar but IIRC it uses system malloc, not jemalloc.

Lee: can you reproduce locally with both values? run: 
```bash
./scripts/run_bench --seq 2048 --concurrency 12 --microbatch-wait 5
./scripts/run_bench --seq 2048 --concurrency 12 --microbatch-wait 10
```
post the outputs if you can.

Maria: running both now, will drop numbers in ~10m.

Sam: my quick read — if p99 is <+5% and RSS <+7% I'm ok merging behind a small canary + tight monitoring. propose canary: 5% traffic, 45m, tracing on.

Sam: @Maria can you sign off when you have the local numbers? I can grant approval after that.

Maria: local run finished: p99=149ms (baseline 148ms), RSS +1%. Looks fine locally. CI bench reproduced the +4% though when run on canary-sim (system malloc). So env variance on allocators.

Alex: good catch. I'll open an infra issue to standardize allocator for bench infra so numbers are comparable.

Sam: OK. I approve conditional on canary plan (5% x45m) and tracers on. @Alex proceed once Maria confirms canary dashboard checks in the first 15m.

Maria: I re-ran a canary-sim local replica and got numbers matching bench-bot (p99 151ms). So this is reproducible in canary-sim specifically. I've added a quick memory + p99 check to the canary dashboard.

Alex: proposed rollout plan: merge, trigger canary 5% for 45m, abort if p99 > +7% or RSS > +9%. I'll add fallback to previous batching default as a fast revert.

Jordan: sounds good. If p99 crosses +7% revert plan in place. I can watch traces during the canary window.

bench-bot: Starting canary run - traffic=5% start_ts=1784123590, monitor=latency,memory,traces.

ci-bot: All checks still green for merge.

Sam: Approved — go ahead @Alex. Merge in the 10:00 UTC window or the earliest after Maria's green.

Alex: Merged PR #5223 and kicked off canary: https://git.internal/pull/5223/merge :rocket:

Jordan: monitoring enabled. will flag immediately if anything spikes.

Maria: I've configured dashboard alerts — p99 threshold set to baseline+7%.

Alex: opening follow-up issue to normalize bench infra allocators and capture this env variance: https://issues.internal/RED-789.

bench-bot: Canary: run started, first 5m sample p99=150ms, RSS=9.8GB.

Alex: will post post-canary summary in this thread when available. Thanks all for quick reviews :heart:
